title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Number of Originals Entered at Issue
content:
This page defines the number of originals entered when a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` record is issued.

## Rule

1. **Number when originals go into circulation.** The number is the document type's number of originals per set. On a type whose per-set number is zero, no originals exist at all, and the number is zero.
2. **Combination.** Every condition under which the issue rules put no originals into circulation stands on its own: if any one of them applies, the number entered is zero, whatever else is true. The per-set number is entered only when none of them applies.
3. **What a zero does not do.** Issue of a document whose cargo is not on board stays barred by the rules on issue, zero or not; the zero records only that no originals would go into circulation.
4. **The prepaid-freight hold.** The hold for unsettled prepaid freight governs whether issue can happen in the first place; it has no bearing on how many originals are entered.
5. **Unit.** The number is a whole count of original documents.

## Truth table

| A condition putting no originals into circulation applies | Number entered |
|---|---|
| Yes | 0 |
| No | Per-set number of the type |

## Hypothetical examples

- Type with a per-set number taken as 3, none of the zero conditions applying: 3 originals entered.
- Same type, one zero condition applying: 0 entered.
- Type with a per-set number of 0: 0 entered in every case.
- A document held at issue for unpaid prepaid freight is not issued; once issued, it enters exactly the same number as it would have without the hold.
